claims.says: Under the config invariant, Rust's GRAPH.QUERY flag parser and C's agree on success or failure and on every flag, for every argument vector Rust does not refuse with a SCHEMA_HASH error.
An RO_QUERY that is not rejected performs no write, and the query contained neither a mutating clause nor a write procedure call.
Every successful GRAPH.CONFIG SET batch, from any starting configuration, leaves TIMEOUT_DEFAULT no greater than TIMEOUT_MAX whenever both are set to positive values.
For any buffer size of at least 9 bytes, well-formed values written by the buffered RDB writer read back exactly, in order, through Redis string buffers, leaving what follows untouched.
For any header, rows and statistics, the compact reply the Rust encoder builds decodes in the falkordb-py parser to the same column names and each cell's intended client value.
